The effect of hedges is the difference between these two figures. The percentage effect is calculated by dividing the effect of hedges by the increase without hedges and multiplying by 100.
- Increase in 2014 annual fuel expense without hedges: $104 million (EVIDENCE [2])
- Increase in 2014 annual fuel expense with hedges: $87 million (EVIDENCE [2])
- Effect of hedges = Increase without hedges - Increase with hedges = $104 million - $87 million = $17 million
- Percentage effect = (Effect of hedges / Increase without hedges) * 100 = ($17 million / $104 million) * 100
